title: Add contract-first RAG smoke lab and docsite tour
author: Maya Torres
description: Motivation: make it easier for teams to validate RAG tool contracts and streaming behavior end-to-end in a small, repeatable smoke lab. This PR introduces a contract-first RAG smoke lab that combines typed tool-contract artifacts, a lightweight local authoring runner, Playwright-based smoke tests for tool-calling flows, and a docsite tour that walks through authoring, contract verification, and common failure modes. Main deliverables: 1) examples/contract-lab/: a minimal RAG example with typed tool schemas, a small incremental index, and a local runner that exercises step-by-step tool-call sequences; 2) tests/smoke/playwright/: Playwright smoke tests that assert tool-call sequences, structured output shape, and graceful streaming resume; 3) docs/rag-contract-lab.md: a docsite page with a guided walkthrough, troubleshooting tips, and CI snippets to enable teams to run the lab in CI. Usage: clone repo, cd examples/contract-lab, yarn install, yarn start to run the local runner; yarn smoke to run Playwright checks. Checklist: [x] example scaffolding and README [x] Playwright smoke tests and CI job [x] docsite tour and quickstart snippets [x] types for tool contracts and CI-friendly fixtures. Related: ENG-1429 covers contract-first tooling work; SUP-501 surfaced a customer bug where streaming responses could truncate during tool handoff. Design notes: the lab intentionally keeps the model stubs small (mocked LLM adapter with deterministic outputs) so CI runs are stable and low-cost; the Playwright tests run against the local runner via a small browser shim to simulate streaming client behavior (delta patches and resumable partial responses). Security: no secrets, uses local indexed JSON blobs; the doc includes a note on swapping in a private indexer and KMS for private deployment. Backwards compatibility: purely additive examples and docs. Migration: N/A. Next steps: add an option to run against Redwood Hosted API for end-to-end baseline comparisons, and expand the contract linters in a follow-up PR.
